name: Barbell Incline Close-Grip Bench Press
summary: An incline pressing variation using a narrow grip to heavily emphasize the triceps and upper chest.

aliases.text: Incline Close Grip Barbell Bench Press

setup: Set an adjustable bench to an incline between 30 and 45 degrees inside a rack.
Lie back on the bench with your eyes directly under the racked bar, planting your feet firmly on the floor.
Grasp the barbell with a pronated grip approximately shoulder-width apart.
Retract and depress your shoulder blades, then unrack the bar and hold it directly above your upper chest with elbows extended.
steps: Inhale and lower the barbell under control toward your upper chest, keeping your elbows tucked at roughly a 30 to 45-degree angle to your torso.
Touch the bar lightly to your chest without bouncing.
Exhale and press the barbell back up along a slight backward arc to the starting position, fully extending your elbows.
instructions.breathing: Inhale as you lower the bar to your chest, hold briefly through the bottom turn, and exhale as you press back to lockout.
cues: Keep elbows tucked rather than flared.
Squeeze the bar tightly and stack your wrists over your elbows.
Drive through your triceps at the top of the press.

common_faults.fault: Gripping the bar excessively narrow (hands touching or only inches apart).
common_faults.correction: Space your hands roughly shoulder-width apart to protect your wrists and optimize triceps leverage.

common_faults.fault: Flaring the elbows outward during the descent.
common_faults.correction: Keep your elbows tucked closer to your ribs to shift load to the triceps and spare the anterior shoulders.

common_faults.fault: Bouncing the bar off the chest.
common_faults.correction: Lower the bar with control and pause momentarily before pressing upward.

precautions: Use safety spotter arms set just above chest height or perform with a competent spotter.
Avoid using a thumbless (false) grip with a narrow hand placement.
